items.stem: A team adds a bigger model to speed up a slow RAG system, but it gets slower and pricier. What step did they skip?

options.text: Profiling to find the actual bottleneck before optimising
options.rationale: Correct: measure first; the bottleneck may not be the model.
Hardware spend without profiling may not help.
Larger top-k usually adds cost and latency.

items.explanation: Correct: measure first; the bottleneck may not be the model.
items.domain_ref: Where latency and cost come from
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO caching practices cut cost without serving wrong answers? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Cache embeddings and retrieval results for repeated inputs
options.rationale: Correct: caching repeated work avoids recomputation safely.

options.text: Invalidate cached answers when their source content changes
options.rationale: Correct: invalidation prevents serving stale answers.

options.text: Cache answers forever with no invalidation
options.rationale: That serves stale, possibly wrong answers.

options.text: Disable caching to guarantee freshness at any cost
options.rationale: That needlessly raises cost and latency.

items.explanation: Correct: caching repeated work avoids recomputation safely.

items.stem: Before shipping a cost-cutting change, what must you verify?

options.text: That answer quality stays within an acceptable threshold on an evaluation set
options.rationale: Correct: cost cuts must not silently degrade quality.

options.text: That the change reduces the codebase size
options.rationale: Code size is not the concern.
Vendor approval is not the gate.
You want latency to drop, and quality to hold.

items.explanation: Correct: cost cuts must not silently degrade quality.
